handbookNote: Minnesota Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Minnesota previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only mn_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Minnesota Department of Commerce. PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading (via a 'Click Here for the Real Estate Candidate Information Bulletin' link found on PSI's own test-taker landing page, test-takers.psiexams.com/mnre) and reading PSI's official Real Estate Salesperson, Broker and Abstracter Examination Candidate Information Bulletin (copyright 2023, updated 10/1/2023, bulletin id 10954). Exam Summary Table, quoted directly from the bulletin: Broker General portion = 75 items (80 points possible -- General broker exams include questions scored up to two points), 2.5 hours; Broker State portion = 60 items (60 points), 1.5 hours; Broker Both = 135 items (140 points combined -- another real source-document arithmetic quirk: 80+60=140 points but 75+60=135 items, both figures are internally consistent on their own terms, not an error like MA's), 4 hours combined. Passing: the bulletin states directly 'You must get 75% correct to pass' -- a flat 75% threshold, not a scaled score. Candidates who pass one portion and fail the other need only retake the failed portion. 5-10 unscored experimental items may also appear. track_registry models this as exam_question_count=135, exam_duration_sec=14400 (240 min), pass_percent=75, min_correct=101 (ceil(135*0.75)=101.25->101, though the real exam likely applies 75% to EACH portion's own point total independently -- 75*0.75=56.25->57 and 60*0.75=45 exactly -- rather than one combined 75% cutoff; this site's single-number track_registry schema uses the whole-track approximation, consistent with every other multi-portion state in this campaign). CONTENT OUTLINE -- General portion percentages, quoted verbatim from the bulletin (Broker column, summing to exactly 100% of the 75-item general portion, independently re-verified by hand this session): Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19% (the largest single national topic), Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% (Broker-only sub-items), Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% (Broker-only supervisory sub-items), Real Estate Calculations 6%. NOTABLE: these percentages are IDENTICAL to every other PSI-administered state in this campaign (NJ/TN/VA/AZ/MA/MO/MD) -- yet further confirmation PSI uses one shared multi-state 'General Portion' content-outline template for real estate broker exams nationwide. Minnesota State Content Outline, quoted verbatim as item counts (Broker column): Real Estate Brokerage License Law 25 items (Definitions Ch. 82.55, Licensing 82.57-82.63, Trust accounts 82.75, Standards of Conduct 82.72-82.73, Commissioner's authority 45.011-45.43, Real Estate Education/Research/Recovery Fund 82.86, Agency Disclosure Requirements 82.67, Other Disclosure Requirements 82.68, Compensation 82.70); Interests in Real Property 10 items (Ownership -- Conveyance by Spouses 507.02/500.19, Subdivided Lands 83.20-83.45, Common interest ownership -- Condominiums Ch. 515/Uniform Condominium Act 515A/Minnesota Common Interest Ownership Act 515B, real estate taxes/special assessments Ch. 279; Landlords and tenants Ch. 504B); Conveyance Procedures and Protection of Parties 9 items (Recording/fees -- Registration/Torrens Ch. 508, Mortgage Registry Tax/Deed Tax Ch. 287; Statutory Home Warranties 327A.02; Minnesota Human Rights Act 363A; Minnesota Statute of Frauds Ch. 513/336.2A-201; Environmental Issues -- septic systems 115.55, wells 103I.235, leaking underground storage tanks 116.46-48/115C.01-09); Financial Instruments: Obligations, Rights, Remedies 6 items (Mortgages/contracts for deed -- Foreclosure by Advertisement Ch. 580, Foreclosure by Action Ch. 581, Foreclosure General Provisions Ch. 582, Contract for deed Sec. 559, Homestead exemptions Ch. 510; Liens -- Labor/Material Ch. 514). REAL SOURCE-DOCUMENT DISCREPANCY FOUND AND FLAGGED (not silently resolved): the bulletin's own 4 state-category item counts (25+10+9+6) sum to exactly 50, not the 60 stated in the Broker State row of the Exam Summary Table -- a genuine 10-item gap in the source document between its own summary table and its own detailed category breakdown. Rather than invent a resolution, this build used the granular 4-category breakdown as-is for proportional bucket sizing (since it is the more detailed, itemized figure) while track_registry's exam_question_count still reflects the summary table's stated 135 combined total, since that is what the real exam actually administers regardless of which of PSI's own internal documents undercounts the state category breakdown. Real Minnesota statute facts independently verified this session via revisor.mn.gov (Minnesota's official Office of the Revisor of Statutes site) -- notably including a live-caught correction: Minn. Stat. 82.011 does not exist (404 on revisor.mn.gov) and was replaced with the correct 82.82 (license discipline) and 45.027 (Commissioner's general enforcement powers) citations for Commissioner's-authority content, and a UCC citation (336.2A-201, governing leases of goods/personal property under Article 2A) was deliberately NOT used for real-property Statute of Frauds content despite being listed in the bulletin's own outline, since it does not actually govern real property conveyances -- Minn. Stat. 513.04/513.05 were used instead as the genuinely applicable real-property Statute of Frauds sections. Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math content not tied to a Minnesota-specific statute is sourced to 'national real estate practice principles' framing throughout. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate. This bank was drafted across 15 parallel single-topic drafting passes (11 national + 4 Minnesota state-law categories), each pass instructed to draft as many genuinely distinct, real, grounded questions as its topic's source material supports with NO target number or ceiling -- the corrected drafting methodology adopted after discovering and fixing a target-anchoring bug in this campaign's earlier NJ/TN/VA/AZ/MA/MO builds (see mo_re_broker.json for the full incident writeup). A cross-bucket source_note-citation dedup check across all 15 files found ZERO cross-bucket near-duplicates -- the cleanest dedup result of any state in this campaign so far. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_mn_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 15 bucket files combined, in file order), producing a final near-even 25.1/25.1/24.9/24.9% A/B/C/D distribution. 642 raw questions drafted against a 135-item exam -- a 4.76:1 pool ratio, comfortably clearing the standing 4:1 new-track floor with no backfill pass needed.
